questions.question_text: Surgical powders are sterilised by :

options.D: Moist heat in presence of bactericide

questions.explanation: Dry heat sterilization is commonly used for surgical powders and thermostable non-aqueous substances as moisture cannot easily penetrate packed powders.

questions.question_text: In an autoclave, water boils at a temperature :
questions.explanation: Due to increased pressure inside an autoclave ($>1\text{ atm}$), water boils at temperatures greater than 100°C.

questions.question_text: Which among the following cannot be used for the sterilisation of packed materials?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet rays have very low penetrating power and cannot effectively penetrate packaging materials to sterilize the contents.

questions.question_text: Advantage of Ethylene oxide sterilisation

options.C: In expensive and low running cost
options.D: Does not damage moisture sensitive substances

questions.explanation: Ethylene oxide is a gas sterilization method used for heat- and moisture-sensitive medical devices.

questions.question_text: Air entrapment among the granules during compression may lead to
questions.explanation: Trapped air within the granules during tablet compression expands after the pressure is released, causing capping or lamination.

questions.question_text: The disintegration time limit for conventional sugar coated tablet :
questions.explanation: Conventional sugar-coated tablets have a pharmacopoeial disintegration time limit of 60 minutes.

questions.question_text: The polymer that can be used for enteric coating :
questions.explanation: Polyvinyl acetate phthalate (PVAP) is an enteric polymer that resists gastric fluid and dissolves in the intestinal fluid.

questions.question_text: After compression, in a conventional tableting machine :

options.A: Upper punch remain stationary, and lower punch moves up
options.B: Upper punch remain stationary and lower punch drops down
options.C: Upper and lower punches move down.
options.D: The upper punch and lower punch move up

questions.explanation: After compression, the upper punch withdraws upward, and the lower punch moves up to eject the tablet from the die cavity.

questions.question_text: The smallest size of capsule shell :
questions.explanation: Capsule sizes range from 000 (largest) to 5 (smallest) for human use.

questions.question_text: Ideally, hard gelatin capsule shell should contain __________% of moisture.
questions.explanation: Hard gelatin capsule shells typically contain 12% to 15% residual moisture to maintain flexibility and prevent brittleness.

questions.question_text: Pick out the correct statement :

options.A: The maximum quantity of eye ointment that can be packed in a single container is 5 gram
options.B: Test for sterility is not mandatory for eye ointments
options.C: Eye ointments should not contain antioxidants
options.D: Eye ointments should not contain preservatives

questions.explanation: According to pharmacopoeial standards, the maximum quantity of eye ointment packed in a single container should not exceed 5 grams to minimize contamination risks.

questions.question_text: pH range of Dextrose injection I.P :
questions.explanation: Dextrose injection I.P. has an acidic pH range of 3.5 to 6.5 to prevent caramelization during heat sterilization.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is an antiperspirant?
questions.explanation: Aluminium chlorohydrate is widely used as an active antiperspirant ingredient in cosmetics to reduce sweat production.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is not an ingredient of liquid paraffin emulsion I.P?
questions.explanation: Sodium benzoate is typically not part of the standard liquid paraffin emulsion formula I.P., which uses chloroform water, gum acacia, tragacanth, and vanillin.

questions.question_text: Which among the following is NOT a cationic emulsifying agent?
questions.explanation: Triethanolamine stearate is an anionic emulsifying agent, whereas the others are quaternary ammonium cationic surfactants.

questions.question_text: Pick out the wrong statement :

options.A: Certain surfactants can be used as flocculating agents
options.B: The effectiveness of an electrolyte in flocculation depends on the valence of its ion
options.C: Sediment is formed rapidly in flocculated suspensions
options.D: Electrolytes added as flocculants should have the same charge as that of the dispersed phase particles

questions.explanation: Electrolytes used as flocculants should carry a charge opposite to that of the dispersed particles to reduce zeta potential and cause flocculation.

questions.question_text: In diffusible solid among the following :
questions.explanation: Rhubarb powder is classified as a diffusible solid, whereas magnesium trisilicate, kaolin, and calamine are indeffusible solids.

questions.question_text: Di calcium phosphate in tooth paste serve as a :
questions.explanation: Dicalcium phosphate is an abrasive polishing agent used in toothpaste formulations.

questions.question_text: Pick out the wrong statement :

options.A: Oily suspensions cannot be given by the IM route
options.B: Oily solutions can be given by the IM route
options.C: Intra thecal injections are injected into sub arachnoid space
options.D: Intra thecal injections should be isotonic

questions.explanation: Oily suspensions and solutions are frequently administered via the intramuscular (IM) route for depot effects, making statement A incorrect.

questions.question_text: Among the following, the preservative concentration allowed in eye drops is lowest for :
questions.explanation: Phenylmercuric nitrate is extremely potent and used at very low concentrations (around 0.001% w/v) compared to others like chlorbutol.

questions.question_text: The calcium compound used topically in the treatment of burns by hydrofluoric acid :
questions.explanation: Calcium gluconate gel is the standard topical treatment for hydrofluoric acid burns to bind fluoride ions.

questions.question_text: Substance added as a stabilizer for aqueous solutions of mild silver protein :
questions.explanation: Disodium edetate (EDTA) is added as a chelating stabilizer to prevent precipitation and oxidation in mild silver protein solutions.

questions.question_text: The concentration of iodine in strong iodine solution I.P. is :
questions.explanation: Strong iodine solution I.P. (Lugol's solution) contains 5% w/v iodine and 10% w/v potassium iodide.

questions.question_text: Tartar emetic is :
questions.explanation: Tartar emetic is chemically antimony potassium tartrate.

questions.question_text: Antidote for iron poisoning is :
questions.explanation: Desferrioxamine is the specific chelating agent used as an antidote for acute iron poisoning.

questions.question_text: Spirit of salt is the synonym for :
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid is historically known by the synonym 'spirit of salt'.

questions.question_text: The content of chlorine in chlorinated lime should be not less than :
questions.explanation: Chlorinated lime (bleaching powder) must contain not less than 30% w/w of available chlorine.

questions.question_text: Sodium nitrite is an example of :
questions.explanation: Sodium nitrite acts as a chemical antidote in cyanide poisoning by converting hemoglobin to methemoglobin, which binds cyanide.

questions.question_text: Drugs which expel bronchial secretions are called :
questions.explanation: Expectorants are agents that help in expelling mucus and bronchial secretions from the respiratory tract.

questions.question_text: Argyria occurs due to excessive deposition of _________ in our body :
questions.explanation: Argyria is a condition caused by excessive accumulation of silver in the body tissues, leading to a blue-gray skin discoloration.

questions.question_text: Drug of choice for treatment of typhoid fever :
questions.explanation: Chloramphenicol is historically recognized as the classic drug of choice for treating typhoid fever caused by Salmonella typhi.

questions.question_text: Co-trimoxazole consists of trimethoprim and sulphamethoxazole in the ratio :
questions.explanation: Co-trimoxazole is a fixed-dose combination containing trimethoprim and sulfamethoxazole in a 1:4 ratio.

questions.question_text: Fluorouracil is a :
questions.explanation: 5-Fluorouracil is an antimetabolite and pyrimidine analogue used in cancer chemotherapy.

questions.question_text: Ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity are the main adverse effects of :
questions.explanation: Aminoglycoside antibiotics like gentamicin are well known for causing ototoxicity and nephrotoxicity.

questions.question_text: Example of Alpha-adrenergic blocker :
questions.explanation: Tolazoline is a non-selective alpha-adrenergic antagonist.

questions.question_text: The antibiotic not produced by the genus streptomyces :
questions.explanation: Gentamicin is produced by Micromonospora purpurea, whereas the others are produced by Streptomyces species.

questions.question_text: All of the following are antimalarial drugs except :
questions.explanation: Pyrazinamide is an antitubercular drug, while the rest are antimalarials.

questions.question_text: Librium is the trade name of :
questions.explanation: Librium is the classic brand name for chlordiazepoxide, the first benzodiazepine.

questions.question_text: ____________ is a cholinesterase reactivator.
questions.explanation: Pralidoxime (2-PAM) acts as a cholinesterase reactivator used in organophosphate poisoning.

questions.question_text: Anti neoplastic antibiotic :
questions.explanation: Dactinomycin (actinomycin D) is an antineoplastic antibiotic used in cancer chemotherapy.

questions.question_text: Commercial source of digoxin :
questions.explanation: Digitalis lanata is the primary commercial source for digoxin and related glycosides.

questions.question_text: Family of Commiphora molmol :
questions.explanation: Commiphora molmol (Myrrh) belongs to the family Burseraceae.

questions.question_text: Sulphuric acid and Forhde’s reagent with emetine gives :
questions.explanation: Emetine with sulfuric acid and Frohde's reagent gives a characteristic pink to red color.

questions.question_text: Crow fig is the synonym of :
questions.explanation: Nux vomica is commonly known as crow fig or poison nut.

questions.question_text: Tinnaveli senna consists of the dried leaf lets of :
questions.explanation: Tinnevelly senna consists of the dried leaflets of Cassia angustifolia.

questions.question_text: The glycoside present in cinchona :
questions.explanation: Quinovin is a bitter glycoside found in Cinchona bark.

questions.question_text: Number of secondary ridges present in fennel :
questions.explanation: Fennel fruit features prominent primary ridges and typically lacks secondary ridges.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a diuretic drug?
questions.explanation: Punarnava (Boerhavia diffusa) is well known in Ayurveda for its diuretic properties.

questions.question_text: Combined umbelliferon test is positive for :
questions.explanation: Asafoetida, also known as devil's dung, gives a positive umbelliferon test due to umbellic acid derivatives.

questions.question_text: Hydnocarpic acid is the main constituent present in :
questions.explanation: Hydnocarpic acid is a cyclic fatty acid characteristic of chaulmoogra oil obtained from Gynocardia / Hydnocarpus species.

questions.question_text: Tranexaemic acid is used in :
questions.explanation: Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic agent commonly used to reduce heavy menstrual bleeding (menorrhagia).

questions.question_text: Clindamycin act by :
questions.explanation: Clindamycin binds to the 50S ribosomal subunit to inhibit bacterial protein synthesis.

questions.question_text: Cheese reaction is associated with :
questions.explanation: The 'cheese reaction' refers to severe hypertensive crisis caused by tyramine-rich foods interacting with MAO inhibitors.

questions.question_text: Drugs or biological products which are used for the diagnosis or treatment of rare diseases are called as :
questions.explanation: Products intended for treating rare diseases are officially designated as orphan drugs.

questions.question_text: The specific antidote of methanol poisoning :
questions.explanation: Fomepizole is an alcohol dehydrogenase inhibitor used as a specific antidote for methanol and ethylene glycol poisoning.

questions.question_text: A purine nucleotide having rapid and short antiarrythmic action :
questions.explanation: Adenosine is an endogenous purine nucleoside used intravenously for its rapid, short-acting antiarrhythmic effects.

questions.question_text: Which is the following is a systemic antacid?
questions.explanation: Sodium bicarbonate is absorbed systemically, unlike most other antacids, classifying it as a systemic antacid.

questions.question_text: Example for loop diuretic is :
questions.explanation: Torsemide is a loop diuretic acting on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Anticholine esterases used for the treatment of alzheimers diseases?
questions.explanation: Tacrine was the first acetylcholinesterase inhibitor approved for treating Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question_text: An example for alpha glucosidase inhibitor hypoglycemic drug :
questions.explanation: Acarbose functions by inhibiting alpha-glucosidase enzymes in the intestinal brush border.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not an ex-officio member of Pharmacy Council of India?

options.A: The Director General of Health Services
options.B: The Director of Central Drug Laboratories

questions.explanation: The Director of Pharmacopoeia Laboratory is not listed as an ex-officio member of the Pharmacy Council of India under the Pharmacy Act.

questions.question_text: The Schedule of Life Period of Drug is:
questions.explanation: Schedule P under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act deals with the life period (expiry date) of drugs.

questions.question_text: The Chairman of the Drug Technical Advisory Board is:

options.B: The Director, Central Drug Laboratory, Kolkata
options.C: The President, Pharmacy Council of India
options.D: The Director General of Health Services

questions.explanation: The Director General of Health Services serves as the chairman of the Drug Technical Advisory Board (DTAB).

questions.question_text: The State Pharmacy Council should have the following no. of elected members:
questions.explanation: A State Pharmacy Council consists of six members elected from among registered pharmacists.

questions.question_text: Schedule ‘D’ as per D&C act is Concerned with:

options.A: List of drugs exempted from the provision of import of drugs
options.B: Diseases and ailments which drug may not purport to prevent or cure

questions.explanation: Schedule D covers the list of drugs exempted from certain provisions regarding import of drugs.

questions.question_text: If a drug contains color which is not prescribed is called :
questions.explanation: A drug bearing a color not permitted or prescribed is legally classified as misbranded.

questions.question_text: Minimum Age Prescribed for registration as Pharmacist is:
questions.explanation: Under the Pharmacy Act, a person must have attained the age of 18 years to be registered as a pharmacist.

questions.question_text: Drug Inspector is appointed under the act of :
questions.explanation: Drug Inspectors are appointed under Section 21 of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act.

questions.question_text: The Drug samples taken by Drug inspector for Analysis are sending to :
questions.explanation: Samples collected by a Drug Inspector are sent to the Government Analyst for examination and test.

questions.question_text: The schedule in D&C Act that deals with the standards of Disinfectant fluids are :
questions.explanation: Schedule O specifies the standards for disinfectant fluids under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act.

questions.question_text: How much is the minimum space required to open a new Drug Store?
questions.explanation: The minimum area required for retail drug store as per standard regulations is 10 square meters (approx. 90-100 sq ft).

questions.question_text: Given the following which is not an ideal place for Opening a New Drug Store :
questions.explanation: Undeveloped or poorly populated areas are generally considered non-ideal compared to high traffic or hospital zones.

questions.question_text: Before allowing Credit, which of the following essential information must be obtained about the Client :
questions.explanation: The 'Three Cs' of credit evaluation are Character, Capacity, and Capital.

questions.question_text: Inventory consists of the following :
questions.explanation: Total business inventory encompasses raw materials, work-in-progress, and finished goods.

questions.question_text: Minimum Stock level is known :
questions.explanation: The minimum stock level acts as a buffer stock to prevent stockouts.

questions.question_text: Bin card is maintained by :
questions.explanation: A bin card is a quantitative record of inventory kept at the store and maintained by the storekeeper.

questions.question_text: The level is below the minimum stock level is called:
questions.explanation: When stock falls below the minimum level, it reaches the danger level requiring emergency action.

questions.question_text: According to perpetual inventory system the record is the following type :
questions.explanation: Perpetual inventory systems maintain continuous records via store ledgers and bin cards.

questions.question_text: Which techniques are used for sale promotion?
questions.explanation: Coupons, fairs, and trading stamps are all recognized sales promotion techniques.

questions.question_text: Mixed Bank is a combination of :

options.C: Exchange Bank and Import Export Bank
options.D: Land development Bank and Savings Bank

questions.explanation: A mixed bank typically combines functions of commercial banking and industrial financing.

questions.question_text: Limulus Ameobocyte lysate test is used to detect :
questions.explanation: The Limulus Amebocyte Lysate (LAL) test is used to detect bacterial endotoxins (pyrogens).

questions.question_text: –––––––––– is considered as suitable containers for parenterals.
questions.explanation: Treated soda-lime glass or surface-treated (silica treated) glass is suitable for certain parenteral formulations.

questions.question_text: The size of multiple dose container parenteral is limited to –––––––––– ml by USP.
questions.explanation: USP limits the volume of multiple-dose parenteral containers to a maximum of 30 ml.

questions.question_text: Cryoprotectants is used in parenterals as :
questions.explanation: Cryoprotectants are added to freeze-dried or frozen preparations to prevent damage during freezing processes.

questions.question_text: Systematic review of randomized control trials is an example of –––––––––– source of drug information.
questions.explanation: Systematic reviews and meta-analyses aggregate primary literature and are classified as secondary sources.

questions.question_text: –––––––––––– is not a WHO drug selection criteria to add new drugs into drug formulary.

options.C: On the WHO essential drug list

questions.explanation: WHO formulary selection generally favors single compounds over fixed-dose combination compounds unless proven synergistic.

questions.question_text: Usually who will be the chairman of pharmacy and therapeutic committee :
questions.explanation: The Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) committee is typically chaired by a physician, often representing the medical staff, working collaboratively with pharmacists and other healthcare professionals.

questions.question_text: Pharmacy and therapeutic committee should meet regularly atleast –––––––––– times in a year.
questions.explanation: The Pharmacy and Therapeutics committee generally meets at least quarterly (4 times a year) to ensure proper medication management and hospital formulary updates.

questions.question_text: Complete floor stock system is an example of –––––––––– drug distribution.
questions.explanation: Floor stock systems are a traditional method used within inpatient hospital settings for distributing medications directly to nursing units.

questions.question_text: In inventory control the term Reserve stock means :

options.B: Excess usage requirement during normal lead time
options.C: Stock for usage at normal late

questions.explanation: Reserve stock, or safety stock, refers to the minimum stock level maintained in inventory to prevent stockouts during unexpected delays or surges.

questions.question_text: __________ is a cause of pharmaco dynamic drug interactions.
questions.explanation: Receptor site interactions involve pharmacodynamic mechanisms where drugs directly affect each other's actions at the target site.

questions.question_text: __________ is associated with the withdrawal of a medicine.
questions.explanation: Type E adverse drug reactions are associated with the withdrawal or cessation of a drug (e.g., withdrawal syndrome).

questions.question_text: __________ is an example of category X drugs for pregnancy.
questions.explanation: Isotretinoin is a potent teratogen classified under pregnancy Category X due to severe risks of fetal abnormalities.

questions.question_text: Poor bio availability means the drug is :
questions.explanation: Highly ionized drugs have poor lipid solubility, leading to difficulties in crossing biological membranes and poor bioavailability.

questions.question_text: First line antidote for beta blocker toxicity is :
questions.explanation: Glucagon bypasses beta-receptors by increasing intracellular cyclic AMP, making it the first-line antidote for beta-blocker overdose.

questions.question_text: Normal HbA1C level is __________
questions.explanation: A normal glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) level for individuals without diabetes is generally considered to be below 5.7% (or 5.6%).

questions.question_text: A person is stage II hypertensive if his BP is __________ as per JNC-7 classification.
questions.explanation: According to the JNC-7 classification, Stage 2 hypertension is defined as a systolic blood pressure $\ge 160$ mmHg or a diastolic blood pressure $\ge 100$ mmHg.

questions.question_text: Coma cocktail antidote refers to Intravenous administration of :
questions.explanation: The traditional coma cocktail consists of intravenous administration of dextrose, naloxone, and thiamine for patients with altered mental status.

questions.question_text: __________ is the antidote for organophosphates poisoning.
questions.explanation: Anticholinergics such as atropine are used as antidotes to counteract the excessive cholinergic effects caused by organophosphate poisoning.

questions.question_text: Urea breath test is to diagnose :
questions.explanation: The urea breath test detects the presence of Helicobacter pylori by measuring labeled carbon dioxide in the breath after ingestion of labeled urea.
